issue.title: Command chips: one-gesture bob runs from Obsidian notes
issue.description: Typing `run: bob …` in an inline code span, or a `bob-run` fence, gives a quiet ▶ chip. One click or ⌘↵ runs it through Bob Command Mode the way the sheet's Ctrl+Enter would. A chip holds one command or a whole `&&` sequence, and its run state shows in place. The copy-chip plugin becomes `bob-chips` and owns both kinds, and the GTD rows that hold bob commands become command chips.

payload.entry: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: copyChipSerialize can emit a bob-copy fence that an indented body line closes early — it counts fence runs only at column 0, so text "a\n  ```\nb" serializes with a ``` marker and the "  ```" body line closes it (payload truncates to "a"). runChipSerialize avoids this with closerAware; copy was left byte-stable for C11. Fix by counting runs after leading whitespace, update copy vectors deliberately, and re-pin COPY_VECTORS_SHA256 in scripts/test-command-chips-grammar.cjs.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: commandChipAt only shields run chips inside math and comments that open on the same line. A run chip inside a multi-line %% / <!-- --> comment block or a $$ block that opened on an earlier line still resolves for ⌘↵ (Live Preview hides it via the syntax tree, the pure rule does not). The keymap phase (bob-cli-nu.6) or a small follow-up should track cross-line comment and math state in commandChipAt, outside fences.

Shared one-pass chipScanLine (kind-tagged copy|run; run spans also skip same-line math and %%/HTML comments); copyChipScanLine is now its copy filter. runChipParseContent / runChipScanLine / runChipParseFenceInfo / runChipSerialize (bob-run fence; refuses a block in a table cell; fence marker outruns indented closer-like lines); chipLinkSpans (md links and images, wikilinks and embeds, autolinks, bare http(s) URLs, outside code spans); commandChipAt implements rules 1-7 with frozen none / ambiguous{via,message} / ready{via,chip}; block chips carry fence:{open,close}; task scan generalized as chipScanTaskScope. api.commandChips v1 (version, parse, scanLine, parseFenceInfo, fencePayload, serialize, chipAt) beside the unchanged copyChips v2, plus a fallback namespace. payload.entry: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Chips on nested list bullets never render in Live Preview — bob-chips 050-live-preview.js copyChipLiveLineIsIndentedCode (/^(?: {4}|\t)\S/) treats every tab- or 4-space-indented line, i.e. every nested bullet such as "\t- `run: bob plan`", as an indented code block, so chipLiveChipsForLine returns [] for both copy and command chips there (Reading view is unaffected). Fix idea: when the syntax tree is available, rely on copyChipLivePosIsInlineCode (which already rejects codeblock nodes) and keep the regex only as the tree-less fallback, or skip it for list-item continuation lines; add LP vectors for tab- and 4-space-nested bullets.
